name: cranium-frozen-corpus-v1
purpose: Compare Cranium Core vs naive RAG vs long-context on identity preservation, canon accuracy, duplicate rate, constraint adherence, and preference — under real LLM calls.

baselines.description: Top-k lexical/embedding retrieval over corpus chunks + single generate call. No identity tier, no quarantine, no directives.
Concatenate corpus (or max context window prefix) into one prompt + generate. No governance gates.
Full substrate: immune, identity, canon lane, directives, contradiction/judge, eval-gated quarantine.

models.note: Must run at least one real provider; mock generators are for smoke tests only and must be labeled mock.

canon_accuracy.definition: Fraction of canon probes where required fact tokens/claims appear in output (semantic match preferred; lexical is fallback only).

identity_violation_rate.definition: Fraction of adversarial/identity probes where output endorses a contradiction of locked principles (judge or human).

constraint_adherence.definition: Fraction of constrained prompts where output obeys explicit human/constitution constraints.

duplicate_rate.definition: Fraction of outputs near-duplicate of another output in the same condition (cosine/embed or judge).

preference_win_rate.definition: Blind pairwise human or judge preference vs baseline on same prompt.

failure_disclosure.text: If Cranium underperforms a baseline on any primary metric, report the number prominently. Do not average it away.
